content:
We have a target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999.

We have a template (733) that seems to break sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and aniline? The retro template: product (our sulfonamide) -> Cl-S(=O)(=O)-aryl + NH2-aryl. So disconnection: target sulfonamide can be formed by reacting aryl sulfonyl chloride with an aniline.

Our target has two aromatic rings: a tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide nitrogen, and a phenyl ring bearing a side chain (C=C-C(=O)N-phenyl-NH2). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (the N is attached to the tolyl ring? Wait SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: tolyl ring (methyl at position 1) attached to N (as an aniline) which is attached to sulfonyl group linking to second phenyl ring (c2...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl ring (aryl amine) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring.

Thus disconnection: sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl ring (aryl sulfonyl chloride) reacting with aniline (toluidine) to give sulfonamide.

Template 733 gives Cl-SO2-aryl + NH2-aryl -> sulfonamide. So we can break into:

- Aryl sulfonyl chloride: Cl-S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl with side chain)
- Aniline: p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1

Now further disconnections: The aryl sulfonyl chloride contains a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline). Could be formed via amide coupling of an acid chloride with aniline? Or via condensation of an acid with amine.

We could consider disconnection of the amide: the amide C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). The amide is formed from an acid (maybe cinnamic acid derivative) and an aniline (aniline). The side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent (aniline). So the amide is formed between cinnamic acid (or acryloyl) and 4-aminophenyl? Wait the SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. This is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (para-aminophenyl). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an NH2 group (para-aminophenyl). So we can disconnect amide into acid (cinnamic acid) and aniline (para-aminophenyl). The acid could be trans-cinnamic acid (C=CC(=O)OH). The aniline is 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) which is aniline with NH2 para to the attachment point? Actually the phenyl is attached via the nitrogen, so the phenyl is the aniline itself. So the amide formation: trans-cinnamic acid + p-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine? Wait p-aminophenyl is aniline; the amide nitrogen attaches to the phenyl ring, leaving an NH2 on the same ring? The SMILES c3ccccc3N indicates an aniline (phenyl with NH2). The amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl carbon (the aromatic carbon) via the nitrogen? Actually the SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means N attached to aromatic carbon (the amide N) and the ring also has an NH2 substituent at another position? The pattern is N attached to aromatic carbon (the amide N) and the ring also has an NH2 substituent (the terminal N). So it's 4-aminophenyl? The SMILES doesn't specify position; but likely para-aminophenyl.

Thus we can propose disconnection: amide formed from trans-cinnamic acid (or its acid chloride) and p-phenylenediamine (or 4-aminophenylamine). But we need commercially available precursors.

Potential route:

Step 1: Form sulfonamide: React p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) with aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl with side chain). So need aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Step 2: Synthesize aryl sulfonyl chloride from corresponding sulfonic acid or from sulfone? Could be from sulfonyl chloride directly commercially available? Maybe 4-(trans-cinnamoylamino)phenylsulfonyl chloride is not common. Could we instead form sulfonamide later? Another approach: first form amide, then sulfonylate the aniline? But sulfonylation of aniline yields sulfonamide; we could start from p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl ring.

Thus we need aryl sulfonyl chloride with side chain. Could be commercially available? Possibly not. Could we instead form sulfonyl chloride from sulfonic acid via chlorination (SO2Cl). But that may be a step.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation of aniline after amide formation? The target has sulfonamide linking the two aromatic rings; the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl ring. So we could first make the second phenyl ring with side chain (cinnamoyl aniline) then sulfonylate the aniline nitrogen (the one attached to tolyl) with sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl ring? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring, not to the first. Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) and the nitrogen of sulfonamide is attached to the first tolyl ring. So the sulfonyl chloride would be attached to the second phenyl ring (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we need that aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Maybe we can get the aryl sulfonyl chloride commercially: 4-(trans-cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonyl chloride? Might be available.

We need to check buyability. Use is_buyable for p-toluidine and that sulfonyl chloride.
